title: Even neighborhoods away from hills remain at risk of Fourth of July fires
text:

Starting tomorrow night, fireworks will fly in certain areas of Utah. Many cities in Utah have banned them for fire danger, but there are still areas where they can be set off legally.
Five Davis County cities ban private fireworks amid heightened wildfire risk And while some might disagree with even that, you can't control other people, but you can control how you protect yourself and your home. Firefighters have been preaching about defensible space for years, but some might think it's mostly meant for those out in the country. But wildfires aren't the only risk when it comes to fireworks; fires can start right in the middle of a neighborhood.
"We had about a 30-foot fireball going up with black smoke everywhere in the neighborhood,” Mortimer told 2News after the incident. "Anything that you can reduce the fuel for the fire is going to benefit you,” said Skyler Henson with Prime Landscaping. While mowing, weed whacking, and just cleaning up are quick and effective ways to take care of things, Henson said you can get long-term built-in mitigation from landscaping.
"Especially with the fires and at the time, water restrictions because of how dry the winter was, and they're thinking, ‘What can we do? ’" Henson said landscaping can help create long-term safety by creating that defensible space, adding things like sprinklers, or even xeriscaping, which Mortimer did after his close call.
"You can really make things nice around the property, and it doesn't have to be ugly. It can look good, it can be intentional, and it can kill two birds with one stone,” Henson said. He said it’s possible to be decorative, cost-effective, and both water and fire-wise all at the same time. Just last week, Sandy City Fire highlighted homeowners whose mitigation efforts helped save their home when a fire started nearby.
